## Prepare dog names
{{< include dog-names.qmd >}}

## Prepare baby names
{{< include baby-names.qmd >}}

## Mark names recorded in the baby-name reference
The distinct-name reference has one row per formatted name found in the selected SSA records. Mark those reference names TRUE before looking them up for each dog. This means the name appears somewhere in the published 1880–2019 records; it does not require a top-100 ranking.
```{r}
#| label: mark-recorded-baby-names
all_distinct_baby_names |>
  mutate(name_appears_in_ssa = TRUE) ->
  baby_name_recognition_reference

baby_name_recognition_reference |>
  preview()
```

## Look up each dog's name
Join on the formatted name. A left join keeps every prepared dog, including dogs whose names do not appear in the reference. Because the reference has one row per name, this lookup does not multiply dog rows. Dog sex and birth year are not join keys: the reference covers both baby sex categories and the whole selected period.
```{r}
#| label: look-up-dog-name-recognition
dogs_prepared |>
  left_join(baby_name_recognition_reference, by = "name") ->
  dogs_with_name_lookup
```

## Mark names with no reference match
An unmatched dog has a missing lookup result. `replace_na()` changes those missing answers to FALSE, leaving the matched TRUE answers alone. It comes from tidyr, loaded with tidyverse. FALSE means absent from our selected published records, not proof that nobody has received the name.
```{r}
#| label: mark-unmatched-dog-names
dogs_with_name_lookup |>
  mutate(name_appears_in_ssa = replace_na(name_appears_in_ssa, FALSE)) ->
  dogs_with_name_recognition

# Show three examples of each result, where available.
dogs_with_name_recognition |>
  select(source_row_id, name, name_appears_in_ssa) |>
  group_by(name_appears_in_ssa) |>
  slice_head(n = 3) |>
  ungroup()
```

## Collect each name's top-100 decades
The reference currently has one row per name and qualifying decade. Sort the decades, group by name, and use `list(decade)` to collect each name's decades into one cell. This produces one lookup row per name so attaching it will not repeat dog rows. The values inside the cell remain numbers, not comma-separated text.
```{r}
#| label: collect-top100-decades
baby_names_top100_by_decade_prepared |>
  arrange(name, decade) |>
  group_by(name) |>
  summarise(top100_decades = list(decade)) |>
  ungroup() ->
  baby_names_top100_decade_lists

baby_names_top100_decade_lists |>
  preview()
```

## Attach the top-100 decades to dogs
Keep every dog with a left join on name. An unmatched list-cell is NULL, meaning there are no qualifying decades in this reference. A name can appear in SSA while never entering a top-100 list; name recognition and top-100 membership answer different questions.
```{r}
#| label: attach-top100-decades
dogs_with_name_recognition |>
  left_join(baby_names_top100_decade_lists, by = "name") ->
  dogs_with_top100_decades

dogs_with_top100_decades |>
  select(source_row_id, name, name_appears_in_ssa, top100_decades) |>
  preview()
```

## Collect each name's peak birth-count decades
The peak reference retains all tied maxima. Collect those decades into a list so every tied peak remains available without creating extra dog rows. Birth counts remain available in the original baby-name reference.
```{r}
#| label: collect-peak-birth-count-decades
baby_names_peak_birth_count_decade |>
  arrange(name, peak_birth_count_decade) |>
  group_by(name) |>
  summarise(peak_birth_count_decades = list(peak_birth_count_decade)) |>
  ungroup() ->
  baby_names_peak_decade_lists

baby_names_peak_decade_lists |>
  preview()
```

## Attach the peak birth-count decades
```{r}
#| label: attach-peak-birth-count-decades
dogs_with_top100_decades |>
  left_join(baby_names_peak_decade_lists, by = "name") ->
  dogs_with_peak_decades

dogs_with_peak_decades |>
  select(source_row_id, name, peak_birth_count_decades) |>
  preview()
```

## Collect each name's highest-ranked decades
Collect every decade sharing the name's highest rank (smallest rank number). This is distinct from the peak birth-count measure: ranking compares the name with other names within each decade.
```{r}
#| label: collect-best-rank-decades
baby_names_best_rank_decade |>
  arrange(name, decade) |>
  group_by(name) |>
  summarise(best_rank_decades = list(decade)) |>
  ungroup() ->
  baby_names_best_rank_decade_lists

baby_names_best_rank_decade_lists |>
  preview()
```

## Attach the highest-ranked decades
```{r}
#| label: attach-best-rank-decades
dogs_with_peak_decades |>
  left_join(baby_names_best_rank_decade_lists, by = "name") ->
  dogs_with_ranked_decades

dogs_with_ranked_decades |>
  select(source_row_id, name, best_rank_decades) |>
  preview()
```

## Attach the weighted average baby birth year
The average-year reference already has one row per name. Rename its value to `average_baby_birth_year` in this lookup to distinguish it from the dog's own `birth_year`.
```{r}
#| label: name-average-baby-year-for-matching
baby_names_average_birth_year |>
  rename(average_baby_birth_year = average_birth_year) ->
  baby_name_average_year_reference
```

```{r}
#| label: finish-dog-baby-name-measures
dogs_with_ranked_decades |>
  left_join(baby_name_average_year_reference, by = "name") ->
  dogs_with_baby_name_measures

dogs_with_baby_name_measures |>
  preview()
```

This is the finished dog–baby table for the final analysis: one row per estimated dog, with the original dog fields, name recognition, three decade lists and weighted average baby birth year. Names absent from the selected SSA records have FALSE recognition, NULL decade lists and an NA average year. NULL lists contain no matches; NA means no average could be supplied. Neither means zero. Income is attached later in the shared final analysis.

## Inspect the contents of a decade list
For display only, expand the top-100 lists of three matched dogs. `unnest()` repeats the dog's identifiers beside each matching decade. The saved final table remains one row per dog. When analyzing shares later, use the full dog population for denominators rather than just these matching rows; unnesting empty lists normally drops those rows.
```{r}
#| label: inspect-matched-decade-values
dogs_with_baby_name_measures |>
  filter(name %in% baby_names_top100_decade_lists$name) |>
  slice_head(n = 3) |>
  select(source_row_id, name, top100_decades) |>
  unnest(top100_decades)
```
